items.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: he said Ricky Woodard. I can’t see it, but I listen to Ricky and there is this saxophone player... But he says, “Ricky Woodard sounds like you.”

ctx.x: Do you think there are young students out today that emulate you?

Ahhh, listen, you know what? I don’t know. There was a friend of mine — in Los Angeles there’s is a young fellow, he says, “He sounds like you.” I said, “Well no, he doesn’t have the sound.” He said, “No, but the stuff that he plays and the phrasing,” he said Ricky Woodard. I can’t see it, but I listen to Ricky and there is this saxophone player, what’s his name — Wilbur Brown. Now Wilbur Brown is a hell of a saxophone player. He lives in L.A. But he says, “Ricky Woodard sounds like you.” I say, “Well not for…

I wanted to ask you about, you know there’s different places in the country where ideas seem to gel collectively for musicians. And Milt Fillius asked us to ask you about Central Avenue, and the things that were going on and the people that you played with.
